messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: checked in bounds code
parts:
I checked in the bounds code. I'll re-LaTeX the manual
and post it on the site.

I tested here with g++ and with clang++, and
everything's fine.

But the build's broken on Jenkins. I'm hoping this
is just a temporary glitch (as we've seen before)
and not an issue with the magic complexity boundary
beyond which the Windows versions of g++ keels over.

It's taking just over 3 GB to compile the revised parser
on my machine in g++, even at -O0.

The problem is with names we get optionality and
order invariance, so we want to allow all of

real<lower=L>
real<upper=U>
real<lower=L,upper=U>
real<upper=U,lower=L>

which makes the syntax in the grammar for the variable
declarations rather more complicated than it used to be.

In the worst case, to support Windows, I may have to back
off the syntax to

real<bounds=[L,U]>

Argh. Every time I touch the syntax it takes me days
to crawl out of the mess it creates in the models, doc
and tests. This Boost parser framework is just WAY too
compiler intensive for its own good (it's an ongoing
issue on the mailing list, needless to say -- we're not the
only ones suffering).

- Bob

parts:
Cool, I'm not sure it's the right model for the data anyway.

The workaround you suggest might be "ugly and wasteful" in one sense,
but it's sort of an elegant hack.

A couple more questions about matrix syntax:
1. Do we not have any way of selecting a column of a matrix?
2. Is there any cleaner way to apply multi_normal_log to the rows of a
matrix than the following?

for (m in 1:M) {
vector[N] ym;
for (n in 1:N)
ym[n] <- y[m,n];
ym ~ multi_normal(mu, Sigma);
}

When I try to do any of the following I get errors:

for (m in 1:M) {
y[m] ~ multi_normal(mu, Sigma);
}

for (m in 1:M) {
y[m]' ~ multi_normal(mu, Sigma);
}

for (m in 1:M) {
vector[N] ym;
ym <- y[m]';
ym ~ multi_normal(mu, Sigma);
}

the problem being that multi_normal wants vectors, not row_vectors,
and it doesn't seem to be possible to directly assign a row_vector to
a vector.

I can attack some of these problems if they aren't already solved.

Matt

On Fri, Aug 17, 2012 at 8:03 PM, Matt Hoffman <mdho...@cs.princeton.edu> wrote:
Cool, I'm not sure it's the right model for the data anyway.

The workaround you suggest might be "ugly and wasteful" in one sense,
but it's sort of an elegant hack.

You can also do the parameter transform yourself.  I.E.,

parameters {
  matrix[4,5] log_A;
}

transformed parameters {
  matrix[4,5] A;
  A <- exp(log_A);
}

Not sure which approach is faster.

A couple more questions about matrix syntax:
1. Do we not have any way of selecting a column of a matrix?
col(A,i) will get you a column and row(A,i) a row but they result in a copy because we're not propagating the Eigen templates.

2. Is there any cleaner way to apply multi_normal_log to the rows of a
matrix than the following?

for (m in 1:M) {
  vector[N] ym;
  for (n in 1:N)
    ym[n] <- y[m,n];
  ym ~ multi_normal(mu, Sigma);
}

When I try to do any of the following I get errors:

for (m in 1:M) {
  y[m] ~ multi_normal(mu, Sigma);
}

for (m in 1:M) {
  y[m]' ~ multi_normal(mu, Sigma);
}

for (m in 1:M) {
  vector[N] ym;
  ym <- y[m]';
  ym ~ multi_normal(mu, Sigma);
}

the problem being that multi_normal wants vectors, not row_vectors,
and it doesn't seem to be possible to directly assign a row_vector to
a vector.

You could probably do

row(y,m)' ~ multi_normal(mu,Sigma);

However, as I noted above, it involves a copy so it may not be any faster than your brute force approach.  That said, it should hopefully become faster at some point in the future :)

Cheers,
Marcus

I can attack some of these problems if they aren't already solved.

Matt

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] checked in bounds code
parts:
There were and still are some glitches in the parser.

Short story, I just pushed a patch so that
you can write, with the parens around y[m] required,

(y[m])' ~ multi_normal(mu,Sigma); // OK, compiles to right thing

Longer story below.

On 8/17/12 8:03 PM, Matt Hoffman wrote:
> Cool, I'm not sure it's the right model for the data anyway.
>
> The workaround you suggest might be "ugly and wasteful" in one sense,
> but it's sort of an elegant hack.

Well, it beats defining your own Jacobians, if
that's what you mean :-)

> A couple more questions about matrix syntax:
> 1. Do we not have any way of selecting a column of a matrix?
> 2. Is there any cleaner way to apply multi_normal_log to the rows of a
> matrix than the following?
>
> for (m in 1:M) {
> vector[N] ym;
> for (n in 1:N)
> ym[n] <- y[m,n];
> ym ~ multi_normal(mu, Sigma);
> }

> When I try to do any of the following I get errors:
>
> for (m in 1:M) {
> y[m] ~ multi_normal(mu, Sigma);
> }

>
> for (m in 1:M) {
> y[m]' ~ multi_normal(mu, Sigma);
> }

This second one should work, with an emphasis
on "should".

y[m] should give you row m of the matrix
as a row vector. Clearly something's wrong.
Here's my whole test program:

data {
int<lower=0> M;
int<lower=0> N;
matrix[M,N] y;
}
parameters {
vector[N] mu;
cov_matrix[N] sigma;
}
model {

for (m in 1:M)
y[m]' ~ multi_normal(mu,Sigma);
}

Aha, as soon as I entered it, I figured out what's
wrong. I misspelled "transpose" in the function_signatures.
Ouch.

Even worse, when I fixed that, it brought up bigger
issues. The syntax

y[m]' ~ multi_normal(mu,Sigma); // FAILS, should be OK

isn't working. I need to write

(y[m])' ~ multi_normal(mu,Sigma); // OK, compiles to right thing

It's clearly down in the expression grammar, not the
statement grammar, because it also doesn't work to do:

(y[m]') ~ multi_normal(mu,Sigma); // FAILS, should be OK

I'll look into it.

Rather than transposing (which causes an alloc and copies,
but no auto-dif -- we're still not using Eigen's expression
templates), you could rearrange your matrix. If it's
data, that could be done in transformed data.

> for (m in 1:M) {
> vector[N] ym;
> ym <- y[m]';
> ym ~ multi_normal(mu, Sigma);
> }
>
> the problem being that multi_normal wants vectors, not row_vectors,
> and it doesn't seem to be possible to directly assign a row_vector to
> a vector.
>
> I can attack some of these problems if they aren't already solved.

What do you think is the right thing to do?
Allow row vectors as arguments to multi normal?

- Bob

parts: On 8/17/12 8:10 PM, Marcus Brubaker wrote:

> On Fri, Aug 17, 2012 at 8:03 PM, Matt Hoffman <mdho...@cs.princeton.edu <mailto:mdho...@cs.princeton.edu>> wrote:

> matrix[4,5] log_A;
> }
>
> transformed parameters {
> matrix[4,5] A;
> A <- exp(log_A);
> }
>
> Not sure which approach is faster.

For parameters, you'll also need the Jacobian (unless
you like the effect of the change of variables on
your prior).

Doing it yourself saves the alloc/assignment cost. The
cost of the transform and Jacobian will be the same.

- Bob

messages.author: 1004dd6f66bb10c3
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] checked in bounds code
parts:
Thanks for looking into this.

I'd be pretty comfortable with allowing row vectors to be arguments to
multi_normal. I think it's pretty unambiguous—if someone passes a row
vector to multi_normal_log() that's of the right size then it's pretty
clear what they meant to do. That would also get around the issue of
having to copy when transposing.

At the risk of parroting Andrew, it's pretty cool to be able to use
Stan for research!

Matt
